problems.source_says: The reported quantitative outcome counts participants whose designs contain the light-ring concept: 18 of 30 students. The observation underlying this proportion is a student, so participant is the supported unit for the reported rate; aggregation into a percentage does not make each observation a whole condition pool. The diversity construct and across_people question remain appropriate because the repeated concept occurs across different students.
problems.quote: is a common idea among AI groups, with 18 out of 30 students (60%) coming up with this concept.
problems.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.2, Homogenization of results; creativity-codebook.md Section 6, Unit.

problems.source_says: Figure 5 compares two pooled condition sets, sketch A+C and AI B+D. For the coded set-level category-coverage outcome, n_units is 2 (derived by counting these two pools), whereas 380 = 89 + 291 counts the constituent ideas. The idea total is supported as corpus size but is incompatible with n_units when unit is set.
problems.quote: two bubble charts comparing idea categories between the sketch groups (left) and the AI groups (right).
problems.locator: PDF p. 8, Figure 5 and caption; p. 7, Section 4.2.3, total ideas and category aggregation; creativity-codebook.md Sections 6 (Unit) and 7 (n_units).

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds: three design professors with more than 10 years of experience used CAT to rate participants’ image concepts and explanatory text on a 1–5 creativity scale; these are expert assessments of produced output.

All six recorded outcomes concern the same design exercise, with AI available in the AI arm and devices prohibited in the sketch arm. S1-O1–O4 therefore answer with_ai; the across-person diversity outcomes S1-O5–O6 answer across_people. No post-removal outcome is reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4–5, Sections 3.2.2–3.2.3 and opening of Section 4.2; pp. 6–8, Sections 4.2.1–4.2.3; codebook Sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 correctly uses overall_creativity, expert_raters, output, and 115 units: 71 sketch concepts and 44 AI concepts. Variations of one AI idea count as one concept; discarded abstract images are excluded. Reverse-order re-rating and ICC 0.67, 95% CI [0.55, 0.76], are stated.
All S1-O1 Table 1 values match: sketch/AI means 2.52/2.89, medians 2.67/3.00, and low through high rating percentages 18.3/9.1, 52.1/29.5, 26.8/54.5, and 2.8/6.8.

Both S1-O1 t-test contrasts reproduce every printed n, mean, SD, t, df, p, d, and confidence limit. The conflicting group letters and d = 0.60 with CI [-0.98, -0.47] are source inconsistencies already disclosed in the form, not transcription errors.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.1; compare p. 4, Section 3.2.2.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 is output-derived fluency counted per participant: 71 image ideas from 31 sketch students versus 44 from 30 AI students, with printed means 2.2 versus 1.4. The form preserves the paper’s means exactly.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.2.3, first paragraph; p. 4, Section 3.2.3.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 correctly counts total text-and-image ideas per participant: sketch 89 and mean 2.8, AI 291 and mean 9.7. The example of one AI participant obtaining 41 descriptive-text ideas is also printed.

S1-O4 correctly codes flexibility, category_count, and participant: researchers sorted each participant’s ideas into themes, and the printed mean categories per student are AI 4,2 versus sketch 2. Within-person variety is flexibility under the codebook.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.2.3; creativity-codebook.md Section 6, Construct and Measure.

confirmed.statement: S1-O5 is based on inspected designs, not the exit survey: the paper reports 18/30 AI students (60%) sharing the light-ring concept and qualitatively describes greater image diversity in the sketch groups. The form correctly treats greater homogenization as lower diversity and does not invent a sketch-arm count.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.2; p. 7, Figure 4 and Section 4.2.3.

confirmed.statement: S1-O6 correctly concerns pooled category diversity across students, uses category_count and set, and distinguishes total-idea coverage from final-image homogenization. Figure 5 visibly covers 9 sketch categories and 12 AI categories, with J–L absent from sketches.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.2.3; p. 8, Figure 5, inspected directly; p. 11, Section 5.1.

confirmed.statement: Every S1-O6 bubble value matches Figure 5: sketch A16 B26 C2 D29 E6 F5 G3 H1 I1, none in J–L; AI A83 B39 C2 D59 E9 F4 G3 H5 I4 J30 K22 L31. Their sums are 89 and 291.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Figure 5, inspected directly; p. 7, Section 4.2.3, printed totals.

confirmed.statement: No additional qualifying AI-versus-control output outcome was found. AUT precedes the intervention; its within-arm correlations are already acknowledged in the form’s notes. Diagnostic/exit opinions are self-reported, and design-path/prompt-style classifications describe process rather than scored creative products. The complete 473-line conversion was read through the references; the 14-page PDF contains no appendix.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 3–5, Sections 3.2.1 and 4.1; p. 7, Section 4.2.4; pp. 8–11, Sections 4.2.5–4.3; pp. 13–14, end matter.

summary: The coding is refuted by the set unit assigned to a participant-level homogenization rate and by 380 ideas recorded as the number of sets for category coverage. Criterion 3 still holds because experts rated participants’ produced designs, and the reported outcome numbers match the PDF.
